summary.one_liner: OpenHands Agent Canvas is a self-hosted developer control center that runs the OpenHands agent and third-party coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Pi, OpenCode, ACP agents) across local, Docker, VM, or cloud backends.
summary.what_it_does: Agent Canvas is a frontend and local stack for starting coding-agent conversations and running automations. The npm package (@openhands/agent-canvas) or a Docker image launches a web UI plus an Agent Server that runs the OpenHands agent by default, and it can drive Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Pi, OpenCode, or any Agent-Client Protocol agent. Each Agent Server runs on one host and port, and the UI can connect to several and switch between them, such as a laptop plus a shared team server. Optional Docker mode gives each new conversation its own container with mounted workspace and persisted state. An Automation Server runs agents on a schedule or in response to webhooks, with integrations described for Slack, GitHub, Linear, and Notion, such as publishing reports to Slack or decomposing GitHub issues into tasks. The README also describes the split into separate repositories for the frontend, SDK/Agent Server, TypeScript client, and automation service.
use_cases: run coding agents on a home or cloud server
switch between local and remote agent backends
schedule recurring agent reports posted to Slack
decompose GitHub issues into tasks automatically
run several coding agents concurrently in Docker containers
share a team agent server for code review and dependency updates
how_to_run: git clone <repo> && cd OpenHands && npm ci && npm run dev
notable: Runs one UI against multiple agent backends (local, Docker, VM, cloud, enterprise) and switches between them
Per-conversation Docker containers with workspace and state mounted, so files survive container replacement
Supports OpenHands plus third-party agents including Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Pi, and OpenCode via ACP
Automation layer that runs on a schedule or from webhook events, integrating with Slack, GitHub, Linear, Notion
caveats: Default no-sandbox install runs the agent server directly on the host with full filesystem access
Exposing the UI beyond loopback requires manual API key entry and self-hosting security hardening per the docs
Source builds need npm 11.12.1 and Node.js 24; Windows setup is in a separate README.windows.md
Docker-per-conversation mode isolates conversation execution only, not the whole Canvas or automation service; existing local conversations are not converted
